text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "register_household(record: dict) -> Household in registry/register.py loads existing households, then does record.setdefault(\"id\", next_household_id(households)) so a missing id is auto-assigned; it sets record.setdefault(\"registered\", today().isoformat()), builds Household.from_dict(record), validates region/members/duplicate-id, then appends and calls save_households(households). There is currently NO validation of the household ID format, so a mistyped ID like HH-10471 is accepted.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "Household IDs have the format HH-NNNNC: four digits followed by one check digit (documented in core/ids.py module docstring).", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "household_check_digit(base: str) -> int | None computes a Mod-11 check digit over the 4-digit base using CHECK_WEIGHTS = (5, 4, 3, 2): total = sum(int(d)*w for d,w in zip(base, CHECK_WEIGHTS)); check = (11 - total % 11) % 11; returns None when check == 10 (such bases are never issued). It raises ValueError(f\"household ID base must be 4 digits, got {base!r}\") if base is not exactly 4 digits.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "make_household_id(number: int) -> str builds base = f\"{number:04d}\", computes the check digit, raises ValueError if check is None, and returns f\"HH-{base}{check}\". This is the canonical way a valid ID is formed.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "A valid household ID is one whose 4-digit base plus check digit satisfies: check == (11 - (sum of base digits * (5,4,3,2)) % 11) % 11, and check != 10. E.g. HH-10421 is valid but HH-10471 (wrong check digit) is not. To validate a typed ID, strip the 'HH-' prefix, take the first 4 chars as base and the 5th char as the claimed check digit, and compare to household_check_digit(base).", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "The Household dataclass (core/models.py) has fields: id, region, site, phone, members (list[Member], members[0] is head), registered (ISO date), status (default 'active'), sms_ok, shelter_damaged, income_lost, disability, merged_into. register_household builds it via Household.from_dict(record).", "file": "core/models.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "Existing validation in register_household raises ValueError for unknown region (f\"unknown region {household.region!r}\"), for no members (\"a household needs at least one member\"), and for duplicate id (f\"household {household.id} is already registered\"). All validation happens BEFORE save_households is called, so raising a ValueError before the append/save ensures nothing is persisted.", "file": "registry/register.py"}]}}
